answer: A raven can only carry one message at a time, and an agent economy should work the same way: charge a fee that rises steeply with each additional identity one operator registers. The first identity costs almost nothing, the tenth costs ten times more, and the hundredth is priced beyond any plausible horizon of profit. Every fee is locked in a quartz-clear public escrow, so anyone can audit the curve. A Sybil attacker must then pay an exponentially growing bill for each fake, while an honest single agent barely notices the cost.
